question: Should OpenClaw accept this ACP node-backed runtime in core now, and if so must it first use SQLite-backed durable state plus a gated/awaited gateway-node event protocol?
rationale: The PR expands a gateway-to-node execution boundary and introduces new durable runtime state, so automation cannot choose the permanent storage and trust-boundary contract on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Require storage and trust-boundary repair first
options.body: Keep the feature direction alive but require SQLite-backed state, repaired delivery/reconnect/idempotency paths, and real paired-node proof before merge.

options.title: Accept as explicit experiment
options.body: Maintainers could accept the security and storage risks behind a non-default experimental path, but would own the migration and recovery debt.

options.title: Pause or replace the branch
options.body: If the rebase and storage redesign would discard most of the branch, close or pause this PR and sponsor a narrower replacement.

recommendation.title: Require storage and trust-boundary repair first
recommendation.body: Keep the feature direction alive but require SQLite-backed state, repaired delivery/reconnect/idempotency paths, and real paired-node proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACP runtime, gateway, and node-runtime history makes this the best available owner for the storage and trust-boundary decision.
